---
title: "How fast is the cane toad moving west?"
format: html
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
```

The records are from every source in `data-raw/sources/`.

```{r}
#| label: counts
tar_read(toads_source_count)
tar_read(gg_decade_count)
```

Each source's own front: the mean position of its 10 westernmost records in each decade. Each one stops where its source stops.

```{r}
#| label: source-fronts
tar_read(source_fronts) |>
  group_by(source) |>
  summarise(
    decades = n(),
    furthest_west = min(lon)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

The front from every source together.

```{r}
#| label: distances
tar_read(toad_distances) |>
  select(decade, lon, lat, distance_km)

tar_read(gg_distances)
```

A straight line through the front, in degrees of longitude per year:

```{r}
#| label: model
coef(tar_read(front_model))
```

```{r}
#| label: maps
tar_read(gg_decades)
tar_read(gg_front)
```

Where could they go? A logistic regression of the records against random background points, on annual mean temperature and annual rainfall. The toad is still spreading, so this shows where it has been recorded, which is less than everywhere it could live.

```{r}
#| label: suitability
tar_read(gg_suitability_map)
```
